title: A Winter for the Room
premise: Ines Galloway's late-night radio show becomes an impossible confessional when the callers turn out to be townspeople who died the previous week, all asking him to 'put it back.' Digging through his grandmother's photographs, Ines finds an extra chair in every image after 1974—the year his family took something from the Hollis well to survive a brutal winter. As the chair moves closer to him in each photo and the dead callers grow more insistent, Ines learns his grandmother traded a neighbor's daughter for their survival and has kept her name out of every record since. Ines returns the stolen ledger of names to the well on the winter solstice, offering his own name alongside it, and survives by becoming a story the town finally tells aloud; the chair remains in the photographs, but now it is empty.
about_author: Isandro Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-market radio producer who spent a decade reading obituaries on air and never quite stopped listening for replies. He writes horror about archives, grief, and the small betrayals that hold families together.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, hosts his 2 a.m. call-in show when a caller describes her own funeral from last Tuesday. He assumes a prank, but her details are exact, and she ends with 'put it back.' Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into dread.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, transcribes the calls obsessively in a notebook, a habit from his grandmother. Three more dead listeners call, each gentler than the last, none angry. Emotional beat: the strange comfort of ritual against the wrongness of the evidence.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, digitizes his late grandmother's photo albums and finds a wooden chair in every image after 1974—always unoccupied, always closer to the camera. His mother claims she's never seen it. Emotional beat: gaslit unease turning to certainty.

chapters.title: Hollis Road
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, drives to the abandoned Hollis property where a capped stone well sits behind dead orchards. He photographs it; the chair appears in the photo, facing the well. Emotional beat: the story reaching for him personally.

chapters.title: Caller Number Nine
chapters.summary: Dual POV: a dead caller named Ruthie narrates her last living day in 1974 while Ines listens, realizing she is describing his grandmother's kitchen. Emotional beat: intimacy with a voice that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, searches the sealed attic and finds a ledger with names crossed out and one page torn away, dated December 1974. The chair in the family photos now sits at his own table. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as debt.

chapters.title: Loyalty
chapters.summary: Mother's POV, a chapter of her refusing to help, revealing she has known since childhood and chose silence to protect the family name. Emotional beat: love expressed as complicity, and its cost.

chapters.title: The Town That Agreed
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, interviews surviving elders who all repeat the same phrase—'that winter, we all got smaller'—and all deny a Hollis daughter ever existed. Emotional beat: collective lie as a living organism.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, returns to the well and finds the cap cracked and the ground warm despite hard frost. The dead callers now speak in unison on his show. Emotional beat: countdown pressure; the well is filling.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Side of the Tape
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV, 1974: the Hollis family starving, the Galloway grandmother arriving with an offer and a ledger. Emotional beat: betrayal rendered as bureaucracy, chillingly polite.

chapters.title: The Photograph That Moves
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, wakes to find the chair beside his bed in every photo in the house, including ones taken this morning. His reflection in the TV sits in it. Emotional beat: the haunting stops being about the past.

chapters.title: Confession on Air
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, breaks format and tells his listeners the truth live; the switchboard lights up with the dead, guiding him, while the living hang up one by one. Emotional beat: exposure as both relief and danger.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Mother's POV, finally surrendering the missing ledger page she has kept in a Bible for fifty years—Ruthie Hollis's name, and Ines's grandmother's signature as witness. Emotional beat: shame handed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Signed
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, tracks down descendants of the eleven signatories; several have died this week, and each house contains a chair. Emotional beat: guilt is generational and it is collecting.

chapters.title: The Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV, present tense from inside the well: not torment but waiting, patient and enormous, counting names until the ledger is whole. Emotional beat: the horror reframes—she isn't vengeful, she is unfinished.

chapters.title: Offerings
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, tries substitutes—photographs, recordings, a written apology buried at the well—and each is rejected, returned on his doorstep wet. Emotional beat: the price cannot be paid in proxy.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, understands at last: the ledger held the town's names, and taking it made the town forget Ruthie ever existed; survival was purchased with erasure. Returning it means everyone remembers everything. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—truth versus loyalty.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, solstice eve: the dead fill the radio waves, the town's elders gather at Ines's door, and the chair sits in the middle of the studio. Emotional beat: held breath before the choice.

chapters.title: Put It Back
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, carries the ledger to the well through a snowfall that falls upward, reads every name aloud, and adds his own at the bottom. The well takes the book and the chair arrives beside him. Emotional beat: sacrifice without melodrama.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, dawn: he is alive, his name gone from every record but the ledger's, remembered only by those who heard the broadcast. Ruthie's voice thanks him once and goes quiet. Emotional beat: grief and grace entwined.

chapters.title: A Winter for the Room
chapters.summary: Mother's POV, weeks later: the town holds its first memorial for Ruthie Hollis; photographs still show the chair, but empty, and no one wants it removed. Emotional beat: truth as the only loyalty that holds.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, hosts his final broadcast, reading the ledger's names as a memorial instead of a debt, and takes one last call—from a listener who says she'll die next week, and would like someone to listen. Emotional beat: the prayer continues, and this time it is answered.
